name: Keiichi Shibahara
current_role: Representative Director and CEO, Amvis Holdings, Inc. (TSE Prime: 7071)
profile: Medical doctor turned immunology/molecular biology researcher who spent about 20 years in science before founding Amvis in 2013 (Kuwana, Mie) at age 48. Amvis runs 'Ishinkan' hospice-style nursing homes where nurses, not resident physicians, manage care for chronic and terminally ill patients; listed 2019, now on TSE Prime.
interesting_fact: The company name Amvis is coined from 'ambitious vision'. Its Ishinkan model relocated hospital beds into nurse-run facilities, starting with Ishinkan Nabari in 2014.
deep_cut_fact: He is a co-author (with Yasumasa Ishida, Yasutoshi Agata and Nobel laureate Tasuku Honjo) of the 1992 EMBO Journal paper that first described PD-1, the molecule behind today's immune checkpoint cancer drugs; his CEO message calls that his first research.
notes: No personal social accounts found. Best route is via Amvis corporate/IR. Graduated Tokai High School and Nagoya University School of Medicine; Kyoto University graduate studies (Honjo lab era).

name: Fernando Trajano
current_role: Shareholder in Magazine Luiza (Magalu); no public executive role found
profile: Fernando Henrique Borges Trajano belongs to the family that controls Brazilian retailer Magazine Luiza (Magalu), founded in Franca (SP) in 1957. In 2018 his father, Onofre de Paula Trajano (the founder's brother), split his Magalu stake among Fernando and siblings Gisele and Ismael. Forbes Brasil 2026 puts the siblings' joint fortune at R$1.5bn.
interesting_fact: Magalu, often called 'the Amazon of Brazil', grew from a single gift shop in Franca into one of Brazil's largest retailers, and most of its sales now come through e-commerce.
notes: Very private passive heir; no interviews, social accounts or personal contacts found. The Forbes bio is partly wrong: Forbes Brasil says his father is Onofre de Paula Trajano (brother of founder Luiza Trajano Donato), not Luiza Helena Trajano. Age about 50 (Forbes Brasil 2026). Not an operating executive; Frederico Trajano is CEO.

name: Ding Shuibo
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Xtep International Holdings (HKEX: 1368)
profile: Ding Shui Po (丁水波), 55, from Chendai, Jinjiang (Fujian), started in shoemaking in 1987, grew an OEM sports-shoe export business, then founded the group behind the Xtep brand in 1999 and listed it in Hong Kong in 2008. Xtep is now a major Chinese running-focused sportswear group that also owns Saucony and Merrell rights in China.
interesting_fact: He has over 30 years in sportswear and has kept studying throughout: Peking, Tsinghua, CKGSB, CEIBS and Xiamen University EMBA programmes, plus Harvard's Global CEO Program in 2018.
deep_cut_fact: Anta founder Ding Shizhong, his biggest Jinjiang rival, was his classmate: 'Ding Shizhong and I are of the same age; we were classmates and are really good friends,' he told the SCMP.
notes: Also romanised Ding Shui Po. Best route is Xtep media/IR. Xtep sponsors many Chinese marathons, which would be a natural podcast angle.

name: Chen Feng-ming
current_role: Co-founder and (per Hurun) shareholder of Chenbro Micom (TWSE: 8210); no current executive role found
profile: 陳鳳明 co-founded Taiwanese chassis maker Chenbro Micom (勤誠興業) in 1983 with his sister Chen Mei-chi (current chairman) and her husband Chen Lien-chun, on NT$500,000 of start-up capital. He left the company early on. Chenbro is now Taiwan's leading server-chassis supplier, and AI server demand has driven its revenue and market value to record highs.
interesting_fact: Chenbro started in PC cases, landing US computer maker Kaypro as an early customer for its first horizontal case in 1984. In the 1990s it marketed itself with the slogan 'Intel Inside, Chenbro Outside'.
notes: Identity uncertain. Hurun 2026 lists him (with Lee Tsun-yen) under Chenbro, and he is a documented co-founder, but Business Next says he left the company early. Current shareholding and biography not verified; the public face of Chenbro is chairman Chen Mei-chi. Data-center angle: Chenbro makes server chassis for hyperscalers.

name: Deng Xueqin
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Kexing Biopharm (科兴制药, SSE STAR: 688136)
profile: Deng Xueqin (邓学勤), born 1967 and a Shenzhen University graduate, worked in Shenzhen Bao'an's construction bureau before going into business. He built the Zhengzhong (正中) property and industrial-park group, then took control of Shandong Kexing. He has chaired Kexing Biopharm since 2019 and took it public on the STAR Market in 2020. Kexing makes recombinant-protein drugs.
interesting_fact: Kexing's flagship SINOGEN (interferon α1b) is described as China's first original genetically engineered drug. It traces back to a 1989 Shenzhen venture set up to commercialise the work of academician Hou Yunde, the 'father of Chinese interferon'. That venture's vaccine arm became the separate Sinovac.
deep_cut_fact: Before biotech he was a public servant: after Shenzhen University he joined the Bao'an District construction bureau in 1989 and rose to deputy director before leaving to start in real estate.
notes: Hurun lists him with Wen Shaozheng (relationship not verified). Low public profile; best route is Kexing's board office / IR. Don't confuse Kexing Biopharm with Sinovac (科兴生物).

name: Zhao Zhenhong
current_role: Legal representative and shareholder, Guangzhou Zhijing Information Technology (致景科技; Baibu / Quanbu textile platforms)
profile: Zhao Zhenhong (赵振洪) heads Guangzhou-based Zhijing Technology (founded 2013, a Hurun unicorn). It runs Baibu, a B2B fabric-trading app, and Quanbu, a textile industrial-internet platform linking yarn, greige, dyeing and garment factories. Investors include Source Code Capital, Tiger Global, DST Global and CICC Capital.
interesting_fact: Zhijing pitches itself as building a 'textile brain'. It uses big data, cloud computing and IoT to digitise China's fragmented fabric supply chain, from raw materials to garment making.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews or social accounts found. Business registration (via 36Kr) confirms him as legal representative and a shareholder; the founder title comes from Hurun's unicorn list. Best route is via the company.

name: Yu Huiyong
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Pagoda Group (百果园, HKEX: 2411)
profile: Yu Huiyong (余惠勇), born 1968 in Dexing, Jiangxi, studied at Jiangxi Agricultural University and moved to Shenzhen. He founded Pagoda in late 2001 and opened China's first specialised fruit-chain store in 2002. Pagoda grew into China's largest fruit retail chain, with thousands of franchised stores, and listed in Hong Kong in 2023. He remains chairman and has called 2026 its 'year of rebirth'.
interesting_fact: Before Pagoda, while selling for Shenzhen Aidi Green Food, he went to Shandong himself to buy domestic Fuji apples to undercut pricey imports. With home delivery and 27 direct-sale points, that business reached nearly RMB100m in sales in 2001.
deep_cut_fact: His first career was in science: after graduating from Jiangxi Agricultural University in 1991 he did edible-mushroom research at the Jiangxi Academy of Agricultural Sciences before heading to Shenzhen.
notes: Hurun lists him with Xu Yanlin (Pagoda co-founder). Best route is Pagoda corporate/IR via the HKEX-listed company. Avoid 2025 consumer-pricing remarks controversy as a topic.

name: William P Stiritz
current_role: Chairman Emeritus, Post Holdings, Inc. (retired from the board Dec 16, 2025); ~10% shareholder
profile: Bill Stiritz spent more than 30 years at Ralston Purina, as chairman, president and CEO from 1981 to 1997. He became known for spin-offs and buybacks, creating Ralcorp, Energizer and Post Holdings. He chaired Post from its 2012 spin-off, serving as CEO until 2014 and executive chairman until 2016. He retired from the board in December 2025 as chairman emeritus and remains a major shareholder.
interesting_fact: He is one of the eight capital-allocator CEOs profiled in William Thorndike's book 'The Outsiders', for his record at Ralston Purina leading up to its 2001 sale to Nestlé.
deep_cut_fact: While a rising Purina executive he earned a master's in European history from Saint Louis University (1968). He and his wife Susan also created WashU's first endowed professorship in women's studies in 1998.
notes: Born c.1934 and very private; rarely gives interviews. Now retired from Post's board, so Post IR may only forward messages. St. Louis-based.

name: Ioannis Alafouzos
current_role: Chairman, Okeanis Eco Tankers (NYSE/OSE: ECO); also head of SKAI Group, publisher of Kathimerini and owner of Panathinaikos FC
profile: Giannis (Ioannis) Alafouzos, born 1957 in Santorini, is a third-generation Greek shipowner and son of Aristeidis Alafouzos. After Oxford he expanded the family's tanker businesses (Kyklades Maritime, Ermis Maritime). He has chaired Okeanis Eco Tankers, whose CEO is his son Aristidis, since 2018. He built the SKAI media group from a 1989 radio-station purchase and also owns Panathinaikos.
interesting_fact: He founded the social campaign 'Oloi Mazi Boroume' ('Together We Can') in 2010, which ran concerts, food and clothing drives and soup kitchens during Greece's debt crisis. SKAI, Kathimerini and WWF Hellas also set up the Parnitha Observatory to monitor forest restoration.
deep_cut_fact: At Oxford, where he read economics and history, he competed as a 100m sprinter. He is also an internationally decorated sailor, racing yachts under the family name Glafki (e.g. Glafki III, designed by Humphreys Yacht Design).
notes: Commonly known as Giannis Alafouzos. Don't confuse him with his son Themistocles (Kathimerini chairman) or son Aristidis (Okeanis CEO). High-profile media owner in Greece; Okeanis IR is the cleanest route. Avoid football/politics controversies.

name: Jabbok Schlacks
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, EquipmentShare.com Inc (Nasdaq: EQPT), Columbia, Missouri
profile: Jabbok Schlacks co-founded EquipmentShare in 2015 with his brother Willy and three others, after the brothers ran construction and contracting businesses from their teens. The company grew from a peer-to-peer equipment marketplace into a national construction equipment rental, sales and telematics business with 448 locations, and raised about $747m in its January 2026 Nasdaq IPO.
interesting_fact: EquipmentShare's T3 cloud platform tracks over 397,000 construction assets with telematics, GPS and keypads. In 2025 the company opened a $100m Technology and Development Center at its Columbia, Mo. headquarters.
deep_cut_fact: The company began as a weekend pitch: in October 2014 the brothers won Startup Weekend Columbia with a peer-to-peer equipment-sharing idea, then joined Y Combinator's Winter 2015 batch.
notes: Strong fit for the podcast: a Midwest founder story (YC alum, Columbia MO) in construction tech, with exposure to data-center construction demand. Personal social accounts not verified. Web-search quota ran out mid-lane, so press/IR emails were not extracted.

name: Shao Yibo
current_role: Chairman and Co-founder, Evolve (Evolve Foundation / Evolve China), the Shao family's philanthropic organization
profile: Bo Shao (邵亦波), born 1973, studied at Harvard (undergraduate and MBA) and worked at BCG. In 1999 he co-founded the Chinese C2C site EachNet (易趣), sold to eBay in 2003, and then co-founded Matrix Partners China, one of China's leading VC firms. In 2018 he left all commercial activity to focus on philanthropy through Evolve.
interesting_fact: In 2017 he committed US$100m to philanthropy. His Evolve organization funds work on 'the evolution of consciousness' and psychospiritual transformation among business leaders, with divisions in the US and China.
deep_cut_fact: As a Shanghai schoolboy at East China Normal University No. 2 Affiliated High School he was a celebrated maths prodigy, winning more than ten national maths-competition top or first prizes before going to Harvard.
notes: Known in English as Bo Shao. He has left venture capital, so pitch him on founder psychology and wellbeing or philanthropy rather than deals. Evolve's general inbox is the published route.

name: Li Jiaxuan
current_role: Former director and early shareholder, Canaan Inc. (Nasdaq: CAN); current role not found
profile: Jiaxuan Li (李佳轩) is a chip designer who joined Canaan, the bitcoin-mining ASIC maker founded by N.G. Zhang, and became a director in December 2015. At the 2019 Nasdaq IPO he was its largest shareholder by share count (~16%, via the trust vehicle Ouroboros Ltd.). He no longer appears among directors in Canaan's latest 20-F.
interesting_fact: Canaan's IPO prospectus named him, alongside founder Nangeng Zhang, as one of the two senior managers the company's future depended on.
deep_cut_fact: Before Canaan he spent 2010–2013 as an IC engineer at Vimicro, the Chinese fabless multimedia-chip company. He holds a computer-science BS from Harbin Institute of Technology (2008) and a software-engineering master's from Beihang University (2010).
notes: Very low profile. He has apparently left Canaan's board, so the company is probably not a route to him. Relevant to the energy/data-center theme (bitcoin-mining hardware). Around 41 in 2026 (age 34 in the 2019 prospectus).

name: Sun Min
current_role: Listed by Hurun (with chairman Peng Wencheng) as a principal of BOMESC Offshore Engineering (博迈科, SSE: 603727); current title not verified
profile: Sun Min (孙民) appears on the Hurun China list 2019–2021 alongside Peng Wencheng for BOMESC Offshore Engineering. Founded in 1996 in Tianjin's Binhai New Area, BOMESC is a modular EPC contractor that builds topside and process modules for offshore oil and gas (including FPSOs), LNG plants and mining projects. Almost all of its business comes from international clients.
interesting_fact: BOMESC builds huge prefabricated modules in Tianjin for FPSOs, floating LNG, LNG plants and artificial-island production facilities, and ships them to projects in the Middle East, Russia, the Americas, Africa and Australia.
notes: Couldn't verify his role or biography; the company site names only chairman Peng Wencheng. Web-search quota ran out mid-lane. Strong energy/LNG angle if he can be identified; route via BOMESC investor relations.

current_role: Chairman and President, Anhui Anke Biotechnology (Group) Co. (安科生物, SZSE: 300009), Hefei
